sentences.text: Researchers investigated how exosomes, small vesicles released by cells, influence pseudorabies virus spread and blood-brain barrier damage in mice.
After verifying via microscopy that samples contained exosomes rather than whole virus particles, the team found these vesicles carried viral genetic material and infected pig kidney cells.
In a laboratory model of the blood-brain barrier, these exosomes caused the structure to lose its protective function.
When injected into the brains of living animals, the exosomes were associated with nerve damage and increased barrier permeability.
The authors suggest that brain-derived exosomes may represent a previously overlooked mechanism for viral spread and vascular injury.
